claims.text: the hit set holds every reference to afk:adversary over the name forms this pass searched

Today Step 10.5 starts /afk:adversary {NNNN-slug} {app-base-url} in a fresh session or subagent that has not seen the run's reasoning, diff or tests, against an app instance the invoker provisions or execute brings up with app-start-gate.sh.

Execute reads the adversary's verdict only from the spawning call's own result: its hard rule forbids waiting on a completion notification from a child and records a child returning nothing usable as 'no verdict'.

Tainted or env_unreachable makes execute respawn a fresh adversary or restore the app and re-run the gate, capped at 2 re-run attempts (then adversary_fail, or blocked(env_unreachable: …)); critical or high findings have a separate cap of 2 remediation cycles before adversary_fail.

The adversary writes its report to plan/review/{NNNN-slug}-adversary.md, overwriting on a re-run, ends with the ADVERSARY: <verdict> — probed=<n> … [report: <path>] line and an In plain terms line, and edits nothing else.
Whether the ADVERSARY: line ends the report file or only the reply is not stated: 'End with:' follows the report instruction, and the same line is what execute reads from the spawn result.

Mission control reads the report file, never the ADVERSARY: line: gates.py and insights.py glob plan/review/*-adversary.md, read the first 4000 characters and match a 'verdict' label before the token (or a **Verdict:** prose line); progress.py only checks that {subtask}-adversary.md exists.

A report that carries only the contract's ADVERSARY: line has no 'verdict' label, so mission control lists it with an empty verdict; the mismatch exists today and the change neither causes nor fixes it.

Other readers of the adversary's output: the review rollup row mentions an existing adversary report, retro mines plan/review/*-adversary.md and the journal's adversary verdict lines, understand reads {plan-dir}/review/*.md, execute journals `adversary {verdict} …`, review's settle loop routes runtime failures to the gate's remediation path, and preflight only names the adversary step as untouched.

Under the change Step 10.5 loses both halves of its read rule (skills/afk/execute/SKILL.md:135): no spawn call returns the verdict, and the only delivery left is a completion message the rule forbids waiting on. That finished message carries only a format version and a result path (S-231) and goes to the adversary role's report target, which is execute only when the pattern names no other target (S-212, S-235, ADR-0015); only the report target may read the result file (S-239), so execute reads the verdict from the report file only as the report target.

The report file becomes the verdict carrier for the adversary role's report target (S-235, S-239), which is execute when the pattern names none; it must then hold a parseable verdict, and skills/afk/adversary/SKILL.md:40-45 does not require the file to: line 40 names the file and follows it with an 'End with:' that does not say whether the ADVERSARY: line ends the file or the reply, and mission control parses a 'verdict' label that the ADVERSARY: line lacks (gates.py:22).

Step 10.5 has no branch for an adversary that ends without finished: the planned contact agent moves it to lost and messages the requester, while the gate knows only clean, findings, tainted, env_unreachable and never reached.

The respawn cap of 2, the verdict set and the finding classes survive the change, since each re-run becomes a new pane agent and nothing in Step 10.5 counts spawn calls; the CLAUDE.md adversarial-gate lockstep pair therefore does not fire, and the new coupling of finished or report to Step 10.5's verdict read sits outside every declared lockstep.

On the pane path skills/afk/adversary/SKILL.md:40 and CLAUDE.md:160's co-writer entry for the adversary hold, but :51's 'The report is the only output' breaks: the pane adversary does a role's work, since it returns a gate verdict (AC-040), and a role's agent writes the role's running checkpoint while it works (AC-024, S-239). On the S-209 fallback execute writes the report file from the adversary's returned text, so :40 and the co-writer entry become false, and :51 holds unless a TR-1 role agent also writes its checkpoint, which the feature documents do not say.

Every feature-document line that states how the adversary gate works at HEAD agrees with the plugin source, except one research line on review files: the blind diet (PD-GATE; research SP-06, SP-15) matches skills/afk/adversary/SKILL.md:21 and skills/afk/execute/SKILL.md:89, the own report file (PD-GATE) matches skills/afk/adversary/SKILL.md:40, the verdict set (the precedent digest; SP-15) matches skills/afk/adversary/SKILL.md:36-38 and :43, the outcome statuses (the precedent digest; SP-08) match skills/afk/execute/SKILL.md:113-126, and the frontier tier (PL-29) matches DELEGATION.md:45.

A verifier that runs the tiers and then the adversary probe, as the patterns proposal draws it (PATTERNS-PROPOSAL.md:142, :154, :194), cannot fill the adversary step, since running the tiers brings the implementor's tests and their results into its context, which taints the verdict (skills/afk/adversary/SKILL.md:21, skills/afk/execute/SKILL.md:89); the PRD does require that session to be fresh (PRD.md:207) and blind to the diff and the tests (AC-045), and leaves only a new agent for each attempt to S-155.

Step 10.5 would take one of two start paths by where execute runs (S-153): in the contact session it starts the pane agent itself; in any other agent it sends the contact agent a start request (AC-042) and waits for the contact agent's turn to end (ADR-0013). Finished goes to the adversary role's report target, the agent that asked when the pattern names none (S-212, S-228), into the target's pane and then as a copy into the contact agent's inbox (S-235). On the contact-session path with no pattern target the report target is the contact agent itself, whose input box no message may enter and whose messages land in its inbox where a tool delivers only by typing into a pane (AC-046, S-215); neither S-235 nor AC-048 says how the two deliveries apply then.

claims.text: At HEAD Step 10.5 already needs the report file, not only the spawn result: it routes critical and high findings by each finding's class and reports adversary_fail with each finding's class and repro path (skills/afk/execute/SKILL.md:92, :118), while the ADVERSARY: line carries only the verdict and severity counts (skills/afk/adversary/SKILL.md:43); the classes and repro live in the report, at HEAD the adversary's only output (skills/afk/adversary/SKILL.md:40, :51, :55). The change does more than move the verdict token into that file: on the pane path the adversary fills a role (ADR-0013; S-190), and every role writes its running checkpoint while it works (AC-024; S-239), a second output that skills/afk/adversary/SKILL.md:51 does not allow. Read literally, the next agent in that role, the next attempt included (S-155), reads that checkpoint (S-239), so a tainted attempt's checkpoint could carry what tainted it into the fresh attempt Step 10.5 respawns (skills/afk/execute/SKILL.md:93).

The no-verdict gap predates the change: skills/afk/execute/SKILL.md:135 records 'no verdict' when a child returns nothing usable and moves on, and no outcome status maps a Step 10.5 that ran without a verdict (success needs a clean or medium-and-low-only gate, :115; adversary_unrun is a gate never reached, :119). The change adds ways to end without one: a refused start request (AC-042), a finished message whose result path is empty (S-221, S-231), a delivery that answers exit 4 (S-235), and an agent lost with no answer (S-228).

The inline-helper exposure is not Codex-only: autopilot's subtask prompt, which demands the adversarial gate (skills/afk/autopilot/SUBAGENT-PROMPT.md:32), states no nesting depth, and DELEGATION.md:29 makes a child without that statement run its helper work inline on any harness (CAPABILITIES.md:15, PROVIDERS.md:71); the feature SDD records that no stage-skill spawn states its depth (SDD.md:620), and providers/CONFORMANCE.md holds no nesting trial. Read literally, execute under autopilot runs the adversary inline, in a context that has seen the diff and the tests; the pane path moves the start to the contact agent (S-153).

If the plugin's Stop entry fires in a pane adversary's session, each attempt being a plugin-enabled session started in the run's worktree (S-152, S-156), the wiring gate runs over the branch's adds and, on an orphan, blocks the finish and prints the orphaned paths with an order to wire a consumer or write an IOU (hooks/stop-gates.sh:104-108; hooks/wiring-gate.sh:202-210); that puts branch file names into a blind agent's context through a channel its diet does not list (skills/afk/adversary/SKILL.md:21) and asks an agent that edits nothing (:51) to edit. hooks/hooks.json registers no SubagentStop entry, and whether Stop fires at a pane agent's turn end is harness runtime.

A pane is a message channel into the adversary that HEAD lacks: under the change every agent but the contact agent gets its messages in its pane (S-189, S-215), a later message may carry data though never a duty (S-150), and the run refuses only an undeclared talk edge (ADR-0016); at HEAD only the parent reaches a running child, by continuation (PROVIDERS.md:26, providers/CONFORMANCE.md:28). AC-032's clause that with no pattern picked, or no human present, a stage runs as it does today (PRD.md:132) would keep driven runs, where Step 10.5 is mandatory (skills/afk/execute/SKILL.md:32, :97; skills/afk/autopilot/SKILL.md:33), on today's subagent path, while ADR-0013 makes role agents, the gate-verdict returner included, pane agents with no configuration wherever a pane transport exists (ADR-0013:8, :18) and the switch defaults to pane (S-230); the documents do not say which rule governs a driven Step 10.5.
